text:
sahil: running into a weird one — when we POST a batch of 8 vectors to /v1/embeddings, half of the batch returns 200 and half return 401. seen twice in the last hour. request ids: req-9a8b7c3, req-9a8b7c4. can someone help collect repro steps?

quentin: hey @sahil — thanks, can you paste the exact curl you used and confirm whether you gzip the payload or use any proxy that might chunk requests? also which model (name) are you hitting?

sahil: curl we used (redacted key):
```
curl -v -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk.live.xxxxx" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Content-Encoding: gzip" \
  -H "X-Request-ID: req-9a8b7c3" \
  --data-binary @batch8.json
```
batch8.json is an array: {"model":"rwd-embed-v1","input":["t1","t2","t3","t4","t5","t6","t7","t8"]} (we gzip before upload).

ashley: interesting — two quick hypotheses: 1) gzip + some load balancers may split and re-auth per-chunk; ephemeral tokens that refresh could expire mid-request, 2) routing to different inference nodes with different auth cache windows. can you run one more curl but without gzip so we can rule out encoding? also include `-H "X-Debug: 1"` so our gateway will attach a debug-id.

sahil: ok trying now (no gzip):
```
curl -v -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk.live.xxxxx" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-Request-ID: req-9a8b7c5" \
  -H "X-Debug: 1" \
  --data '{"model":"rwd-embed-v1","input":["t1","t2","t3","t4","t5","t6","t7","t8"]}'
```
result: all 8 succeeded (200) for req-9a8b7c5. original gzipped run still failing intermittently.

quentin: good repro — so gzip looks suspicious. dana can you check gateway logs for req-9a8b7c3 / req-9a8b7c4 and see whether we saw token validate errors or chunked-body reassembly errors?

dana: pulling logs now. snippet: 
```
2026-09-11T15:02:12Z gateway node-2 recv chunk(0/3) X-Request-ID=req-9a8b7c3
2026-09-11T15:02:12Z auth: validate_token sk.live.xxxxx -> ok
2026-09-11T15:02:12Z gateway node-3 recv chunk(1/3) X-Request-ID=req-9a8b7c3
2026-09-11T15:02:13Z auth: validate_token sk.live.xxxxx -> expired (age 31s)
2026-09-11T15:02:13Z gateway node-3 return 401 X-Request-ID=req-9a8b7c3
2026-09-11T15:02:13Z gateway node-2 chunk reassembly failed -> partial success
```
looks like the token was valid for the first chunk but expired for the second chunk on a different gateway node. that explains half 200 / half 401.

sahil: wow — we do rotate ephemeral tokens every 30s in our client; didn't realize gzip + chunking could span that window.

ashley: path forward: two repro steps for us to capture and for you to test: 1) reproduce with a very short-lived token (rotate every 30s) and gzip payload -> should see partial 401, 2) reproduce by sending same gzipped file via a single-node route: `curl --resolve api.redwood.ai:443:IP_OF_NODE2 ...` to force same gateway node. can you collect both request-ids and attach the debug bundle (gateway debug id + backend trace id)?

quentin: for support bundle collection, include these in the curl header: `-H "X-Debug: 1" -H "X-Request-ID: <id>"` and once you have failures, run our debug-collector script: `./collect-debug --request-id req-9a8b7c3` and paste the resulting .tar.gz link.

sahil: doing the single-node resolve test now, will upload debug bundle. also tried workaround: created token with 5m TTL -> gzipped uploads succeed.

dana: sounds like workaround confirmed. I'll raise a ticket to add a gateway safeguard: if chunked body arrives across multiple auth validations, attempt a continuous-session check or accept previously validated token for reassembly window. filing ENG-4821.

support-bot: created ticket ENG-4821 and linked logs (req-9a8b7c3, req-9a8b7c4). :white_check_mark:

ashley: thanks @sahil — once you upload the debug bundle (req-9a8b7c3/req-9a8b7c4) paste the link here and we'll triage deeper. if you need an immediate workaround: disable client-side gzip or ensure token TTL > expected upload duration. :thumbsup:

sahil: thanks everyone — sharing bundle in 10m. :pray:
